akhfash:1-1.t: He said ﴿قۤ وَٱلْقُرْآنِ ٱلْمَجِيدِ﴾: an oath upon ﴿قَدْ عَلِمْنَا مَا تَنقُصُ ٱلأَرْضُ مِنْهُمْ﴾ [4].

akhfash:3-3.t: And He said ﴿أَإِذَا مِتْنَا وَكُنَّا تُرَاباً ذَلِكَ رَجْعُ بَعِيدٌ﴾: He did not mention "that it is a return"; that is — and Allah knows best — because it was in answer, as though it had been said to them: "You will return". So they said: "When we have become dust? That is a far return."

akhfash:15-15.t: And He said ﴿بَلْ هُمْ فِي لَبْسٍ﴾ because you say: "لَبَسْتُ عليه لَبْساً" (I confused it for him).

akhfash:16-16.t: And He said ﴿وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ ٱلْوَرِيدِ﴾: He means "more in control of him and nearer to him in power over him".

akhfash:17-17.t: And He said ﴿عَنِ ٱلْيَمِينِ وَعَنِ ٱلشِّمَالِ قَعِيدٌ﴾ and did not say "on the right a seated one and on the left a seated one"; He mentioned one of them and it sufficed, as He said ﴿يُخْرِجُكُمْ طِفْلاً﴾, where the singular sufficed for the plural, and as He said ﴿فَإِن طِبْنَ لَكُمْ عَن شَيْءٍ مِّنْهُ نَفْساً﴾.

daas-irab:1-7.t: ﴿ق﴾ a letter with no grammatical position. ﴿وَالْقُرْآنِ﴾ the wāw is a particle, and of oath [Translator's note: so in the source, «حرف وقسم»; presumably "a particle of oath and genitive"]; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb. ﴿الْمَجِيدِ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa); the answer to the oath is omitted. ﴿بَلْ﴾ a particle of conjunction and digression (iḍrāb). ﴿عَجِبُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿أَنْ﴾ a maṣdar-forming particle governing the accusative. ﴿جاءَهُمْ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl (object). ﴿مُنْذِرٌ﴾ a postponed fāʿil. ﴿مِنْهُمْ﴾ the two are attached to منذر; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from an and what follows it is in the position of the accusative by removal of the preposition (bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ). ﴿فَقالَ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb. ﴿الْكافِرُونَ﴾ its fāʿil. ﴿هذا﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿شَيْءٌ﴾ its khabar (predicate). ﴿عَجِيبٌ﴾ an adjective; the nominal clause is the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿أَإِذا﴾ the hamza is a particle of disapproving interrogation (istifhām inkārī), and idhā is an adverbial conditional particle not governing the jussive. ﴿مِتْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿وَكُنَّا تُراباً﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and kāna, its noun and its khabar; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿ذلِكَ رَجْعٌ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar. ﴿بَعِيدٌ﴾ an adjective. ﴿قَدْ﴾ a particle of verification (taḥqīq). ﴿عَلِمْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿ما﴾ its mafʿūl; the clause is resumptive. ﴿تَنْقُصُ الْأَرْضُ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿مِنْهُمْ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿وَعِنْدَنا﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and an adverb of place attached to an omitted, advanced khabar. ﴿كِتابٌ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ. ﴿حَفِيظٌ﴾ an adjective; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿بَلْ﴾ a particle of digression and transition. ﴿كَذَّبُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿بِالْحَقِّ﴾ the two are attached to the verb; the clause is resumptive. ﴿لَمَّا﴾ adverbial, of time ("when"). ﴿جاءَهُمْ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl, and the fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation. ﴿فَهُمْ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and هم is a mubtadaʾ. ﴿فِي أَمْرٍ﴾ the two are attached to the omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ. ﴿مَرِيجٍ﴾ an adjective; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿أَفَلَمْ﴾ the hamza is a particle of disapproving interrogation, the fāʾ is a particle of resumption, and lam is a jussive particle. ﴿يَنْظُرُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by lam, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿إِلَى السَّماءِ﴾ the two are attached to the verb; the clause is resumptive. ﴿فَوْقَهُمْ﴾ an adverb of place. ﴿كَيْفَ﴾ an interrogative noun, ḥāl. ﴿بَنَيْناها﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl; the clause is a badal (substitute) from السماء. ﴿وَزَيَّنَّاها﴾ conjoined to بنيناها. ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is circumstantial, and mā is negating. ﴿لَها﴾ an advanced khabar. ﴿مِنْ﴾ a redundant (zāʾida) preposition. ﴿فُرُوجٍ﴾ genitive in form, nominative in position, a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿وَالْأَرْضَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and الأرض is accusative by an omitted verb, its implied form being "مددنا الأرض". ﴿مَدَدْناها﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl; the clause is explicative (tafsīriyya) and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَأَلْقَيْنا﴾ conjoined to مددنا. ﴿فِيها﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿رَواسِيَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وَأَنْبَتْنا﴾ conjoined to ألقينا. ﴿فِيها﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿مِنْ كُلِّ﴾ the two are also attached to the verb. ﴿زَوْجٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿بَهِيجٍ﴾ an adjective of زوج.

daas-irab:8-15.t: ﴿تَبْصِرَةً﴾ mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). ﴿وَذِكْرى﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to تبصرة. ﴿لِكُلِّ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) تبصرة. ﴿عَبْدٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿مُنِيبٍ﴾ an adjective of عبد. ﴿وَنَزَّلْنا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿مِنَ السَّماءِ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿ماءً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿مُبارَكاً﴾ an adjective; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿فَأَنْبَتْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿بِهِ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿جَنَّاتٍ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَحَبَّ﴾ conjoined to جنات. ﴿الْحَصِيدِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَالنَّخْلَ﴾ conjoined to جنات. ﴿باسِقاتٍ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative (manṣūb) by the kasra. ﴿لَها﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, an advanced khabar (predicate). ﴿طَلْعٌ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿نَضِيدٌ﴾ an adjective of طلع; the nominal clause is a ḥāl. ﴿رِزْقاً﴾ mafʿūl li-ajlihi, accusative. ﴿لِلْعِبادِ﴾ the two are attached to it. ﴿وَأَحْيَيْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿بِهِ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿بَلْدَةً﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿مَيْتاً﴾ an adjective; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿كَذلِكَ﴾ an advanced khabar. ﴿الْخُرُوجُ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ; the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿كَذَّبَتْ﴾ a past verb. ﴿قَبْلَهُمْ﴾ an adverb. ﴿قَوْمُ﴾ fāʿil. ﴿نُوحٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَأَصْحابُ﴾ conjoined to قوم. ﴿الرَّسِّ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَثَمُودُ﴾ also conjoined. ﴿وَعادٌ وَفِرْعَوْنُ وَإِخْوانُ لُوطٍ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَأَصْحابُ الْأَيْكَةِ وَقَوْمُ تُبَّعٍ﴾ also conjoined. ﴿كُلٌّ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿كَذَّبَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿الرُّسُلَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the verbal clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿فَحَقَّ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb. ﴿وَعِيدِ﴾ its fāʿil, and the omitted yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿أَفَعَيِينا﴾ the hamza is a particle of interrogation, the fāʾ is a particle of resumption, and a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿بِالْخَلْقِ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿الْأَوَّلِ﴾ an adjective; the clause is resumptive. ﴿بَلْ﴾ a particle of conjunction and digression (iḍrāb). ﴿هُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿فِي لَبْسٍ﴾ its khabar; the clause is resumptive. ﴿مِنْ خَلْقٍ﴾ the two are attached to لبس. ﴿جَدِيدٍ﴾ an adjective of خلق.

daas-irab:16-21.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ﴾ the wāw is a particle of oath and genitive, the lām occurs in the answer to the oath, and qad is a particle of verification (taḥqīq). ﴿خَلَقْنَا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿الْإِنْسانَ﴾ its mafʿūl (object); the clause is the answer to an oath and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَنَعْلَمُ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "نحن", and the nominal clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿ما﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿تُوَسْوِسُ﴾ an imperfect verb. ﴿بِهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿نَفْسُهُ﴾ fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of mā. ﴿وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial, and a mubtadaʾ and its khabar; the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿إِلَيْهِ﴾ the two are attached to أقرب. ﴿مِنْ حَبْلِ﴾ the two are also attached to أقرب. ﴿الْوَرِيدِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿إِذْ﴾ an adverb of time. ﴿يَتَلَقَّى﴾ an imperfect verb. ﴿الْمُتَلَقِّيانِ﴾ its fāʿil; the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿عَنِ الْيَمِينِ﴾ an advanced khabar. ﴿وَعَنِ الشِّمالِ﴾ the two are conjoined to what precedes them. ﴿قَعِيدٌ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿ما﴾ negating. ﴿يَلْفِظُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause ما يلفظ is resumptive. ﴿مِنْ قَوْلٍ﴾ a redundant (zāʾid) preposition, and a noun genitive in form, accusative in position, mafʿūl bihi. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿لَدَيْهِ﴾ an adverb of place attached to an omitted, advanced khabar. ﴿رَقِيبٌ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ. ﴿عَتِيدٌ﴾ badal (substitute); the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿وَجاءَتْ﴾ the wāw is a particle of resumption, and a past verb. ﴿سَكْرَةُ﴾ fāʿil. ﴿الْمَوْتِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿بِالْحَقِّ﴾ the two are attached to the verb; the clause is resumptive. ﴿ذلِكَ ما﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar; the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿كُنْتَ﴾ kāna and its noun. ﴿مِنْهُ﴾ the two are attached to تحيد. ﴿تَحِيدُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the verbal clause is the khabar of كنت, and the clause كنت is the ṣila of mā and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَنُفِخَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a passive past verb. ﴿فِي الصُّورِ﴾ the two are attached to the verb; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿ذلِكَ يَوْمُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar. ﴿الْوَعِيدِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿وَجاءَتْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a past verb. ﴿كُلُّ﴾ fāʿil. ﴿نَفْسٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿مَعَها﴾ an advanced khabar. ﴿سائِقٌ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ. ﴿وَشَهِيدٌ﴾ conjoined to سائق; the nominal clause is an adjective (ṣifa) of كل.

daas-irab:22-28.t: ﴿لَقَدْ﴾ the lām occurs in the answer to the omitted oath, and qad is a particle of verification (taḥqīq). ﴿كُنْتَ﴾ kāna and its noun. ﴿فِي غَفْلَةٍ﴾ its khabar (predicate); the clause is the answer to the oath and has no grammatical position. ﴿مِنْ هذا﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) غفلة. ﴿فَكَشَفْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿عَنْكَ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿غِطاءَكَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿فَبَصَرُكَ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿الْيَوْمَ﴾ an adverb of time. ﴿حَدِيدٌ﴾ khabar; the clause is also conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَقالَ قَرِينُهُ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿هذا ما﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar; the nominal clause is the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿لَدَيَّ﴾ an adverb of place. ﴿عَتِيدٌ﴾ an adjective of mā. ﴿أَلْقِيا﴾ an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the alif is its fāʿil. ﴿فِي جَهَنَّمَ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿كُلَّ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿كَفَّارٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿عَنِيدٍ﴾ an adjective of كفار; the verbal clause is the object of saying. ﴿مَنَّاعٍ﴾ a second adjective of كفار. ﴿لِلْخَيْرِ﴾ the two are attached to مناع. ﴿مُعْتَدٍ مُرِيبٍ﴾ two further adjectives of كفار. ﴿الَّذِي﴾ badal (substitute) from كل. ﴿جَعَلَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿مَعَ﴾ an adverb of place. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿إِلهاً﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿آخَرَ﴾ an adjective. ﴿فَأَلْقِياهُ﴾ the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (fāʾ of elucidation), and an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn; the alif is its fāʿil and the hāʾ its mafʿūl; the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied (muqaddar) condition and has no grammatical position. ﴿فِي الْعَذابِ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿الشَّدِيدِ﴾ an adjective. ﴿قالَ قَرِينُهُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿رَبَّنا﴾ a vocative (munādā) in construct. ﴿ما﴾ negating. ﴿أَطْغَيْتُهُ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl; the clause is the object of saying. ﴿وَلكِنْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and lākin is a particle of rectification (istidrāk). ﴿كانَ﴾ an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb whose noun is latent. ﴿فِي ضَلالٍ﴾ the khabar of kāna. ﴿بَعِيدٍ﴾ an adjective; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿قالَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿لا تَخْتَصِمُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the lā of prohibition, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the object of saying, and the clause قال is resumptive. ﴿لَدَيَّ﴾ an adverb of place. ﴿وَقَدْ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and a particle of verification. ﴿قَدَّمْتُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿إِلَيْكُمْ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿بِالْوَعِيدِ﴾ the two are also attached to the verb; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:29-35.t: ﴿ما﴾ negating. ﴿يُبَدَّلُ﴾ a passive imperfect verb. ﴿الْقَوْلُ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). ﴿لَدَيَّ﴾ an adverb of place. ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and mā is negating, operating like laysa. ﴿أَنَا﴾ its noun. ﴿بِظَلَّامٍ﴾ genitive in form, accusative in position, the khabar (predicate) of mā. ﴿لِلْعَبِيدِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ظلام; the clause of mā is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿يَوْمَ﴾ an adverb of time attached to ظلام. ﴿نَقُولُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿لِجَهَنَّمَ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿هَلِ﴾ a particle of interrogation. ﴿امْتَلَأْتِ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿وَتَقُولُ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿هَلِ﴾ a particle of interrogation. ﴿مِنْ مَزِيدٍ﴾ min is a redundant (zāʾid) preposition, and مزيد is genitive in form, nominative in position, a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar is omitted; the clause is the object of saying. ﴿وَأُزْلِفَتِ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a passive past verb. ﴿الْجَنَّةُ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil. ﴿لِلْمُتَّقِينَ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿غَيْرَ﴾ an adverb of place. ﴿بَعِيدٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿هذا ما﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar; the clause is parenthetical (iʿtirāḍiyya) and has no grammatical position. ﴿تُوعَدُونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) and has no grammatical position. ﴿لِكُلِّ﴾ a badal (substitute) from His words للمتقين. ﴿أَوَّابٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿حَفِيظٍ﴾ an adjective. ﴿مَنْ﴾ a badal from كل. ﴿خَشِيَ﴾ a past verb. ﴿الرَّحْمنَ﴾ its mafʿūl (object), and the fāʿil is latent; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿بِالْغَيْبِ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted ḥāl. ﴿وَجاءَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a past verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿بِقَلْبٍ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿مُنِيبٍ﴾ an adjective. ﴿ادْخُلُوها﴾ an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is its fāʿil and hā its mafʿūl; the clause is the object of an omitted saying. ﴿بِسَلامٍ﴾ ḥāl. ﴿ذلِكَ يَوْمُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar. ﴿الْخُلُودِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is resumptive. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ an advanced khabar. ﴿ما﴾ mubtadaʾ; the clause is resumptive. ﴿يَشاؤُنَ﴾ a nominative (marfūʿ) imperfect verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿فِيها﴾ the two are attached to the verb; the clause is the ṣila of mā. ﴿وَلَدَيْنا﴾ an advanced khabar. ﴿مَزِيدٌ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:36-39.t: ﴿وَكَمْ﴾ the wāw is a particle of resumption, and kam is predicative (khabariyya), an advanced mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿أَهْلَكْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive. ﴿قَبْلَهُمْ﴾ an adverb of time. ﴿مِنْ قَرْنٍ﴾ min is a redundant (zāʾid) preposition, and قرن is genitive in form, accusative in position, a tamyīz (specification). ﴿هُمْ أَشَدُّ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); the nominal clause is an adjective of قرن. ﴿مِنْهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) أشد. ﴿بَطْشاً﴾ tamyīz. ﴿فَنَقَّبُوا﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿فِي الْبِلادِ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿هَلْ﴾ a particle of interrogation. ﴿مِنْ مَحِيصٍ﴾ a redundant particle, and محيص is genitive in form, nominative in position, a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted; the clause is resumptive. ﴿إِنَّ﴾ a particle resembling the verb. ﴿فِي ذلِكَ﴾ an advanced khabar. ﴿لَذِكْرى﴾ the lām is the lām of inception (lām al-ibtidāʾ), and ذكرى is the noun of inna; the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿لِمَنْ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted adjective of ذكرى. ﴿كانَ لَهُ﴾ kāna and its advanced khabar. ﴿قَلْبٌ﴾ its postponed noun; the verbal clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of man. ﴿أَوْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿أَلْقَى﴾ a past verb. ﴿السَّمْعَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَهُوَ شَهِيدٌ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and a mubtadaʾ and its khabar; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَلَقَدْ﴾ the wāw is a particle of oath and genitive, the lām occurs in the answer to the oath, and qad is a particle of verification. ﴿خَلَقْنَا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿السَّماواتِ﴾ its mafʿūl. ﴿وَالْأَرْضَ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what preceded; the clause is the answer to the oath and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and mā is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿بَيْنَهُما﴾ an adverb of place. ﴿فِي سِتَّةِ﴾ the two are attached to خلقنا. ﴿أَيَّامٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is circumstantial, and mā is negating. ﴿مَسَّنا﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl. ﴿مِنْ لُغُوبٍ﴾ min is a redundant preposition, and a noun genitive in form, nominative in position, the fāʿil of مسنا; the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿فَاصْبِرْ﴾ the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (fāʾ of elucidation), and an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿عَلى ما﴾ the two are attached to the verb; the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied (muqaddar) condition and has no grammatical position. ﴿يَقُولُونَ﴾ a nominative (marfūʿ) imperfect verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَسَبِّحْ﴾ conjoined to اصبر. ﴿بِحَمْدِ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted ḥāl. ﴿رَبِّكَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿قَبْلَ﴾ an adverb of time. ﴿طُلُوعِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿الشَّمْسِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَقَبْلَ الْغُرُوبِ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:40-45.t: ﴿وَمِنَ اللَّيْلِ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) سبح. ﴿فَسَبِّحْهُ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and an imperative verb and its mafʿūl (object); the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿وَأَدْبارَ﴾ an adverb of time. ﴿السُّجُودِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَاسْتَمِعْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿يَوْمَ﴾ an adverb of time. ﴿يُنادِ﴾ an imperfect verb. ﴿الْمُنادِ﴾ fāʿil; the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿مِنْ مَكانٍ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿قَرِيبٍ﴾ an adjective. ﴿يَوْمَ﴾ a badal (substitute) from يوم. ﴿يَسْمَعُونَ﴾ a nominative (marfūʿ) imperfect verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿الصَّيْحَةَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation. ﴿بِالْحَقِّ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿ذلِكَ يَوْمُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate). ﴿الْخُرُوجِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿إِنَّا﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿نَحْنُ﴾ a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl). ﴿نُحْيِي﴾ an imperfect verb, and the fāʿil is latent; the clause is the khabar of inna. ﴿وَنُمِيتُ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to نحيي. ﴿وَإِلَيْنَا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and إلينا is an advanced khabar. ﴿الْمَصِيرُ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ. ﴿يَوْمَ﴾ a badal from يوم يسمعون. ﴿تَشَقَّقُ﴾ an imperfect verb. ﴿الْأَرْضُ﴾ its fāʿil; the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation. ﴿عَنْهُمْ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿سِراعاً﴾ ḥāl. ﴿ذلِكَ حَشْرٌ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar. ﴿عَلَيْنا﴾ the two are attached to what follows them. ﴿يَسِيرٌ﴾ an adjective of حشر; the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿نَحْنُ أَعْلَمُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar; the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿بِما﴾ the two are attached to أعلم. ﴿يَقُولُونَ﴾ a nominative imperfect verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of mā. ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and mā is negating, operating like laysa. ﴿أَنْتَ﴾ its noun. ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ the two are attached to what follows them. ﴿بِجَبَّارٍ﴾ the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾid) preposition, and جبار is genitive in form, accusative in position, the khabar of mā; the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿فَذَكِّرْ﴾ the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (fāʾ of elucidation), and an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿بِالْقُرْآنِ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿مَنْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿يَخافُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿وَعِيدِ﴾ mafʿūl bihi, and the omitted yāʾ of the speaker is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is the ṣila of man, and the clause ذكر is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition and has no grammatical position.

farraa:1-1.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿قۤ وَٱلْقُرْآنِ ٱلْمَجِيدِ﴾.
Qāf: in it is the meaning by which He swore [181/b]. It is reported that it means "it has been decreed (quḍiya), by Allah", as is said of ḥumma: "it has been decreed, by Allah"; "ḥumma, by Allah" means: it has been decreed.
And it is said that (Qāf) is a mountain surrounding the earth. If it is so, it is as though it is in the position of the nominative, i.e. "it is Qāf, by Allah"; and it [should] have shown its nominative ending, because it would be a noun and not a spelled letter. Perhaps the qāf alone was mentioned from its name, as the poet said:
قلنا لها: قفى، فقالت: قافْ
(We said to her: "Stop!" and she said: "Qāf.")
She mentioned the qāf, meaning the qāf of wuqūf (stopping), i.e. "I am stopping."

farraa:3-3.t:
His saying: ﴿أَإِذَا مِتْنَا وَكُنَّا تُرَاباً﴾.
Speech before which there appears nothing to which this would be an answer; but its meaning is implied. It was only, and Allah knows best: ﴿ق وَالْقُرْآنِ الْمَجِيدِ﴾ "you will surely be raised" after death. So they said: "Shall we be raised when we have become dust?", denying the resurrection; then they said: ﴿ذَلِكَ رَجْعُ بَعِيدٌ﴾, denying it altogether. [And] His saying (بعيد) is as you say to a man who errs in a question: "You have gone a way far from the right", i.e. you have erred.

farraa:4-6.t:
His saying: ﴿قَدْ عَلِمْنَا مَا تَنقُصُ ٱلأَرْضُ مِنْهُمْ﴾: what it consumes of them.
His saying: ﴿فِيۤ أَمْرٍ مَّرِيجٍ﴾.
In error.
His saying: ﴿وَمَا لَهَا مِن فُرُوجٍ﴾.
There is no gap or crack in it.

farraa:9-9.t:
His saying: ﴿وَحَبَّ ٱلْحَصِيدِ﴾.
The grain is the harvested; and it is among what is annexed to itself, like His saying: ﴿إِنَّ هَذا لَهُو حَقُّ الْيَقِين﴾; and like it: ﴿وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ الْوَرِيدِ﴾.
The ḥabl (rope) is the warīd (jugular vein) itself, annexed to itself because the wording of its two names differs. Al-warīd is a vein between the throat and the two neck-tendons (ʿilbāwān).

farraa:10-10.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱلنَّخْلَ بَاسِقَاتٍ﴾.
Tall. One says: "it has grown (basaqa) in height"; so they are the tall palms.
His saying: ﴿لَّهَا طَلْعٌ نَّضِيدٌ﴾.
He means: the palm spathe (kufurrā) while it is in its sheaths, it is naḍīd, i.e. arranged one part over another; when it comes out of its sheaths it is not naḍīd.

farraa:15-15.t:
His saying: ﴿أَفَعَيِينَا بِٱلْخَلْقِ ٱلأَوَّلِ﴾.
He says: how, in their view, should We be wearied by the resurrection when We were not wearied by creating them the first time? Then He said: ﴿بَلْ هُمْ فِي لَبْسٍ مِّنْ خَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ﴾, i.e. they are in error and doubt.

farraa:16-16.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا ٱلإِنسَانَ وَنَعْلَمُ مَا تُوَسْوِسُ بِهِ نَفْسُهُ﴾.
The hāʾ is for ما; and in ما توسوس you may make the hāʾ for the man whom it whispers to, meaning: it whispers to him and talks to him.

farraa:17-17.t:
His saying: ﴿عَنِ ٱلْيَمِينِ وَعَنِ ٱلشِّمَالِ قَعِيدٌ﴾.
It says قعيد and does not say قعيدان (dual). Al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: and Ḥibbān ibn ʿAlī narrated to me, from al-Kalbī, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "seated (qaʿīd) on the right and on the left" means seated ones (quʿūd); so he made qaʿīd a plural, as you make al-rasūl (messenger) for a group and for two. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿إِنَّا رَسُولُ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِين﴾, of Moses and his brother. And the poet said:
ألِكْنى إليها، وخيرُ الرسو * لِ أعلَمُهم بنواحِى الْخَبَرْ
(Be my messenger to her; and the best of messengers is the one most knowing of the sides of the news.)
So he made al-rasūl for the plural. This is one view. And if you wish, you make al-qaʿīd singular, one being sufficient for its companion, as the poet said:
نَحْنُ بما عِندنا، وأنت بما * عندك راضٍ، والرأىُ مختلِفُ
(We with what we have, and you with what you have, are content [rāḍin, singular]; and opinion differs.)
And like it is the saying of al-Farazdaq:
إِنِّى ضَمِنت لمن أتانى ما جَنَى * وأبَى، وَكان وكنت غير غَدُورِ
(I guaranteed to whoever came to me [protection from] what he had committed, and my father [did likewise]; and he was, and I was, not treacherous [ghadūr, singular].)
And he did not say غدورين (dual).

farraa:19-19.t: His saying: ﴿وَجَاءَتْ سَكْرَةُ الْمَوْتِ بِالْحَقِّ﴾. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: سكرة الحق بالموت. If you wish, you mean by (بالحق) that He is Allah, Mighty and Majestic; and if you wish, you make the stupor (al-sakra) the death itself, annexed to itself, as though you said: "the true stupor came with death". And His saying: ﴿سَكْرَةُ الْمَوْتِ بِالْحَقِّ﴾: he says: with the truth which had not been clear to them of the matter of the Hereafter. And the truth may be the death, i.e. the stupor of death came with the reality of death.

farraa:22-22.t:
His saying: ﴿فَبَصَرُكَ ٱلْيَوْمَ حَدِيدٌ﴾.
He says: you used to deny, but today you are knowing, of piercing sight; and sight here is knowledge, not with the eye.

farraa:23-23.t:
His saying: ﴿هَـٰذَا مَا لَدَيَّ عَتِيدٌ﴾.
You put عتيد in the nominative by making it a predicate whose ṣila (relative clause) belongs to ما; and if you wish, you make it resumptive (mustaʾnaf), like His saying: ﴿هَذَا بَعْلِى شَيْخٌ﴾. Had it been accusative, it would have been correct, because هذا and ما are both definite, so العتيد is detached (yuqṭaʿ) from them [as a ḥāl].

farraa:24-24.t:
[182/a] His saying: ﴿أَلْقِيَا فِي جَهَنَّمَ كُلَّ كَفَّارٍ عَنِيدٍ﴾.
The Arabs command the one and the group with what two are commanded, saying to a man: "Get up (قوما, dual) away from us". I heard one of them [say]: "Woe to you! Saddle her (ارحلاها, dual) and drive her (ازجرها, singular)". And one of them recited to me:
فقلت لصاحبى لا تحبسانا * بنزع أصوله، واجتزَّ شيحا
(I said to my companion: "Do not detain us [dual] by pulling up its roots, and cut [singular] some wormwood.")
He said: and it is also transmitted: واجدزّ, meaning واجتز. He said: and Abū Tharwān recited to me:
وإن تزجرانى يا ابن عفان أنزجر * وإن تدعانى أَحْمِ عرضاً ممنَّعاً
(If you two [i.e. you] restrain me, O son of ʿAffān, I am restrained; and if you two leave me, I will defend an honour that is well guarded.)
We think this comes from them because the fewest helpers a man has with his camels and sheep are two; and likewise a travelling company, the fewest they are is three; so the speech to one ran as speech to his two companions. Do you not see that the poets most often say: "O my two companions, O my two friends"? Imruʾ al-Qays said:
خليلىّ، مرّا بِى على أم جندب * نُقضِّى لُبانات الفؤاد المعذب
(My two friends, pass with me by Umm Jundab, that we may fulfil the needs of the tormented heart.)
Then he said:
ألَمْ تَرَ أنى كلما جئت طارقا * وجدت بها طيبا وإن لم تطيب
(Have you [singular] not seen that whenever I came by night, I found fragrance with her, even when she was not perfumed?)
So he said ألم تر, returning to the singular, while the beginning of his speech was to two. He said: and another recited to me:
خليلىّ قوما فى عَطالة فانظرا * أناراً ترى من نحو بابَيْن أو برقا
(My two friends, stand on ʿAṭāla and look: do you [singular] see a fire towards Bābayn, or lightning?)
And some of them [recite]: أنارا نرى.
His saying: ﴿مَا أَطْغَيْتُهُ﴾: the angel who used to write down the evil deeds of the unbeliever says it. That is because the unbeliever said: "He used to hurry me away from repentance"; so he said: "I did not make him transgress, O Lord, but he was astray."

farraa:29-29.t: Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿مَا يُبَدَّلُ ٱلْقَوْلُ لَدَيَّ﴾, i.e. no lie is told before Me, because of His knowledge, Mighty and Majestic, of the unseen of that.

farraa:32-33.t:
His saying: ﴿هَـٰذَا مَا تُوعَدُونَ لِكُلِّ أَوَّابٍ حَفِيظٍ﴾ ﴿مَّنْ خَشِيَ﴾.
If you wish, you make (مَن) genitive, following His saying (لكلّ); and if you wish, you make it resumptive, so it is nominative, with the conditional (jazāʾ) meaning intended: whoever fears the All-Merciful in the unseen, it will be said to him: "Enter Paradise". And (ادْخُلوها) is the apodosis (jawāb) of the condition, before which you have implied the verb of saying, and you made it a verb for the plural because مَن may have the sense of the plural.

farraa:36-36.t:
His saying: ﴿فَنَقَّبُواْ فِي ٱلْبِلاَدِ﴾.
The reading of the readers. He says: they pierced through the lands and travelled in them; so was there for them any escape from death? You imply كان here, as He said: ﴿وَكَأَيِّنْ مِّنْ قَرْيَةٍ هي أَشَدُّ قُوّةً مِّنْ قَرْيَتِكَ الَّتى أَخْرَجَتْكَ أَهْلَكْنَاهُمْ فَلا نَاصِرَ لَهُم﴾, and the meaning is: they had no helper when they were destroyed. And whoever reads: (فَنقِّبوا) فى البلاد, with kasra on the qāf, it is like a threat, i.e. go about in the lands, come and go.

farraa:37-37.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لَذِكْرَىٰ لِمَن كَانَ لَهُ قَلْبٌ﴾.
He says: for whoever has intellect. This is allowed in Arabic: you say "You have no heart", "Your heart is not with you" and "Where has your heart gone?", meaning the intellect in all of that.
His saying: ﴿أَوْ أَلْقَى ٱلسَّمْعَ﴾.
He says: or he lends his hearing to the Book of Allah while he is shahīd, i.e. present, not absent.

farraa:38-38.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَا مَسَّنَا مِن لُّغُوبٍ﴾.
He says: of weariness. That is because the Jews of the people of Medina said: He began the creation of the heavens and the earth on Sunday and finished on Friday, and rested on the Sabbath. So Allah sent down: ﴿وَمَا مَسَّنَا مِن لُّغُوبٍ﴾, belying their saying. Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī read it: من لَغوب, with fatḥa on the lām, and it is anomalous (shādhdh).

farraa:40-40.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمِنَ ٱللَّيْلِ فَسَبِّحْهُ وَأَدْبَارَ ٱلسُّجُودِ﴾.
And إِدبار. Whoever reads وأدبار makes it the plural of dubur: adbār; and they are the two rakʿas after the sunset prayer. That came from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, that he said: [182/b] "وأدبار السجود: the two rakʿas after the sunset prayer"; and ﴿وإِدْبارَ النُّجومِ﴾: the two rakʿas (before the dawn prayer). ʿĀṣim used to give fatḥa to the one in Qāf and kasra to the one in al-Ṭūr; giving both kasra and giving both fatḥa are allowed.

farraa:41-41.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱسْتَمِعْ يَوْمَ يُنَادِ ٱلْمُنَادِ مِن مَّكَانٍ قَرِيبٍ﴾.
It is said that Gabriel, peace be upon him, will come to Jerusalem (Bayt al-Maqdis) and call out for the Gathering; that is His saying: ﴿مِن مَّكَانٍ قَرِيبٍ﴾.

farraa:44-44.t:
His saying: ﴿يَوْمَ تَشَقَّقُ ٱلأَرْضُ عَنْهُمْ سِرَاعاً﴾.
To the place of Gathering; and تُشَقق [is also read]; and the meaning is one, like "the man died (māta)" and "was caused to die (umīta)".

farraa:45-45.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَآ أَنتَ عَلَيْهِمْ بِجَبَّارٍ﴾.
He says: you are not a dominator over them. He put al-jabbār in the position of al-sulṭān (the ruler), from al-jabriyya (compulsion). He said: al-Mufaḍḍal recited to me:
ويوم الحَزن إذ حشَدَت مَعدٌّ * وكان الناسُ إلا نحن دينا عصينا عزمةَ الجبار حتى * صبحنا الجوفَ ألفا مُعْلمينا
(And the Day of al-Ḥazn, when Maʿadd gathered and all people but us were in subjection: we defied the resolve of the jabbār until we came upon al-Jawf in the morning, a thousand men wearing battle-marks.)
By al-jabbār he meant al-Mundhir, because of his rule.
And al-Kalbī said, with his isnad: لستَ عَلَيْهِمْ بجَبّار: he says: you were not sent to compel (tajburahum) them to Islam and guidance; you were sent only as a reminder, so remind. That was before he was commanded to fight them.
The Arabs do not say faʿʿāl from afʿaltu: they do not say "this is a kharrāj" or "a dakhkhāl", meaning mudkhil and mukhrij, from adkhaltu and akhrajtu; they say only dakhkhāl from dakhaltu, and faʿʿāl from faʿaltu. The Arabs have said darrāk from adraktu, but it is anomalous. If you take al-jabbār in this sense [i.e. from ajbara], it is a valid view.
And I have heard some of the Arabs say: "jabarahu ʿalā al-amr", meaning ajbarahu (he compelled him); so al-jabbār from this dialect is sound, meaning: one who subdues them and compels them.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat Qāf
Forty-five verses
﷽
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ق والقُرْآنِ المَجِيدِ﴾: most of the people of the language, and what has come in the tafsīr (exegesis), hold that the treatment of "ق" is the treatment of the letters that come at the beginnings of the suras, such as "ن", "الـم" and "ص"; we have explained that. It is possible that the meaning of "قافْ" is: the matter has been decreed (quḍiya al-amr), just as it was said of "حـم": "حُمَّ الأمْرُ" (the matter has been ordained). Those among the people of the language who said that "ق" means "قُضِيَ الأمْرُ" argued from the poet's saying:
؎قُلْنا لَها قِفِي قالَتْ قافْ ∗∗∗ لا تَحْسَبِي أنّا نَسِينا الإيجافْ
(We said to her: Stop! She said: Qāf [I stop]. Do not think that we have forgotten the hard riding.)
Its meaning is: "she said: I stop". The view of people [generally] is that "قافْ" is the opening of the sura, as we have described. It has come in some tafsīr that "قافْ" is a mountain surrounding the world, made of green ruby, and that the sky is white and has only become green from its greenness — and Allah knows best. The jawāb al-qasam (answer of the oath) in ﴿ق والقُرْآنِ المَجِيدِ﴾ is omitted; ﴿أإذا مِتْنا وكُنّا تُرابًا﴾ [Qāf: 3] indicates it. The meaning — and Allah knows best — is: "By the glorious Qur'an, you will surely be raised", and they marvelled and said: ﴿أإذا مِتْنا وكُنّا تُرابًا﴾ [Qāf: 3], that is: shall we be raised when we have died and become dust? Had "إذا" not been attached (mutaʿalliq) [to something implied], there would be no benefit in the speech.
His saying: ﴿ذَلِكَ رَجْعٌ بَعِيدٌ﴾ [Qāf: 3], that is: it is far-fetched in our view that we should be raised after death. It is also possible that the answer is ﴿قَدْ عَلِمْنا ما تَنْقُصُ الأرْضُ مِنهُمْ﴾ [Qāf: 4], so that the meaning is: "Qāf, by the glorious Qur'an, We have certainly known what the earth diminishes of them", the lām having been omitted because what precedes it compensates for it, as He said: ﴿والشَّمْسِ وضُحاها﴾ [al-Shams: 1] up to His saying: ﴿قَدْ أفْلَحَ مَن زَكّاها﴾ [al-Shams: 9], the meaning being: "لَقَدْ أفْلَحَ مَن زَكّاها". The meaning of "ما تَنَقُصُ الأرْضُ مِنهُمْ" is: "what the earth takes of their flesh".

zajjaj:10-10.t: ﴿والنَّخْلَ باسِقاتٍ لَها طَلْعٌ نَضِيدٌ﴾: its busūq is its tallness. The meaning is: "and We caused these things to grow in it".

zajjaj:11-11.t: His saying: ﴿رِزْقًا لِلْعِبادِ﴾ is accusative in two ways. One of them is in the sense of: "We provided them a provision", because His causing these things to grow is provision. It is also possible that it is a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), the meaning being: "We caused these things to grow for provision". Then He said: ﴿كَذَلِكَ الخُرُوجُ﴾, that is: just as We created these things, We will raise you.

zajjaj:14-14.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كُلٌّ كَذَّبَ الرُّسُلَ فَحَقَّ وعِيدِ﴾, that is: the word of punishment and the threat became due upon him, for those who deny the messengers. Likewise His saying: ﴿فَأنْذَرْتُكم نارًا تَلَظّى﴾ [al-Layl: 14] ﴿لا يَصْلاها إلا الأشْقى﴾ [al-Layl: 15] ﴿الَّذِي كَذَّبَ وتَوَلّى﴾ [al-Layl: 16]

zajjaj:15-15.t:
His saying: ﴿أفَعَيِينا بِالخَلْقِ الأوَّلِ﴾: this is [a question of] affirmation (taqrīr), because they acknowledged that Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, is the Creator, yet denied the resurrection; so He said: ﴿أفَعَيِينا بِالخَلْقِ الأوَّلِ﴾. One says "عَيِيتُ بِالأمْرِ" when you do not know how to go about it, and "أعْيَيْتُ" when you become tired.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿بَلْ هم في لَبْسٍ مِن خَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ﴾, that is: rather they are in confusion concerning the resurrection.

zajjaj:16-16.t:
﴿وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنا الإنْسانَ ونَعْلَمُ ما تُوَسْوِسُ بِهِ نَفْسُهُ﴾, that is: We know what he hides and what he conceals within himself. ﴿وَنَحْنُ أقْرَبُ إلَيْهِ مِن حَبْلِ الوَرِيدِ﴾: "اَلْوَرِيدُ" is a vein on the inside of the neck, and there are two warīds. The poet said:
؎كَأنَّ ورِيداهُ رِشاءا خُلْبِ
(As though his two jugular veins were two ropes of khulb.)
He means: of palm fibre.

zajjaj:17-17.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إذْ يَتَلَقّى المُتَلَقِّيانِ عَنِ اليَمِينِ وعَنِ الشِّمالِ قَعِيدٌ﴾: "اَلْمُتَلَقِّيانِ" (the two receivers) are his two scribes entrusted with him, who receive what he does and record it. The meaning is: "on the right a seated one, and on the left a seated one"; one of them indicates the other, so what was indicated was omitted. Like it is the poet's saying:
؎نَحْنُ بِما عِنْدَنا وأنْتَ بِما عِنْـ ∗∗∗ ـدَكَ راضٍ والرَّأْيُ مُخْتَلِفُ
(We with what we have, and you with what you have, are content, though opinion differs.)
That is: we are content with what we have, and you are content with what you have. And like it also:
؎رَمانِي بِأمْرٍ كُنْتُ مِنهُ ووالِدِي ∗∗∗ بَرِيئًا ومِن أجْلِ الطَّوِيِّ رَمانِي
(He accused me of a thing of which I and my father were innocent; it was because of the well that he accused me.)
The meaning is: he accused me of a thing of which I was innocent, and my father innocent of it.

zajjaj:18-18.t: His saying ﴿عَتِيدٌ﴾: "عَتِيدٌ", that is: firm, constant.

zajjaj:19-19.t: His saying: ﴿وَجاءَتْ سَكْرَةُ المَوْتِ بِالحَقِّ﴾, that is: the stupor came which shows a person that he is dying; ﴿بِالحَقِّ﴾, that is: with the death for which he was created. Some said: "وَجاءَتْ سَكْرَةُ الحَقِّ بِالمَوْتِ" (and the stupor of the truth came with death); it has been related from Abū Bakr, may Allah have mercy on him, and the meaning is the same. It was also said: "اَلْحَقُّ" here is Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He.

zajjaj:21-21.t: His saying: ﴿وَجاءَتْ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ مَعَها سائِقٌ وشَهِيدٌ﴾: it was said in the tafsīr (exegesis): "سائِقٌ" (a driver) who drives it to its place of gathering, "وَشَهِيدٌ" (and a witness) who testifies against it with its deeds. It was also said: "وَشَهِيدٌ" is the deed itself.

zajjaj:22-22.t:
His saying: ﴿لَقَدْ كُنْتَ في غَفْلَةٍ مِن هَذا فَكَشَفْنا عَنْكَ غِطاءَكَ﴾: this is a figurative image (mathal). The meaning is: "you were like one over whom there is a covering and over whose heart there is a veil. ﴿فَبَصَرُكَ اليَوْمَ حَدِيدٌ﴾, that is: your knowledge of the state you are in is penetrating. By this baṣar (sight) the sight of the eye is not meant, just as you say: "فُلانٌ بَصِيرٌ بِالنَّحْوِ، والفِقْهِ" (so-and-so is perceptive in grammar and jurisprudence), meaning "knowledgeable in them", and you do not mean the sight of the eye.
[Translator's note: the quotation marks in the source are not balanced here.]

zajjaj:23-23.t:
His saying: ﴿وَقالَ قَرِينُهُ هَذا ما لَدَيَّ عَتِيدٌ﴾: "ما" is put in the nominative by "هَذا", and "عَتِيدٌ" is a ṣifa (adjective) of "ما", for whoever treats "ما" as indefinite; the meaning is: "this is something with me, ready". Its nominative can also be explained in two ways other than this one: [first,] that "عَتِيدٌ" is nominative by an implied element, as though you said: "هَذا شَيْءٌ لَدَيَّ هو عَتِيدٌ" (this is something with me; it is ready). And you may make it nominative as a khabar (predicate) after a khabar, as you say: "هَذا حُلْوٌ حامِضٌ" (this is sweet-sour), so that the meaning is: "this is something with me, ready". It is also possible that its nominative is as a badal (substitute) for "ما", so that the meaning is: "this is ready".
[Translator's note: the text announces two further ways but then lists three: implied pronoun, second khabar, and badal.]

zajjaj:5-5.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿بَلْ كَذَّبُوا بِالحَقِّ لَمّا جاءَهم فَهم في أمْرٍ مَرِيجٍ﴾: "مَرِيجٍ" means: varying, confused for them. At one time they say of the Prophet ﷺ: "a poet", at another: "a sorcerer", and at another: "one taught [by others]"; this is proof that their affair is marīj, confused for them. Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, pointed them to His power to raise them after death through the immensity of His creation, which proves His oneness and that He has power over all things, and said: ﴿أفَلَمْ يَنْظُرُوا إلى السَّماءِ فَوْقَهم كَيْفَ بَنَيْناها وزَيَّنّاها﴾ [Qāf: 6] — and that Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, holds it without pillars from falling upon the earth — ﴿وَما لَها مِن فُرُوجٍ﴾ [Qāf: 6]: there is no crack in it and no gap. ﴿والأرْضَ مَدَدْناها وألْقَيْنا فِيها رَواسِيَ﴾ [Qāf: 7]: "اَلرَّواسِي" are the mountains. ﴿وَأنْبَتْنا فِيها مِن كُلِّ زَوْجٍ بَهِيجٍ﴾ [Qāf: 7] ﴿تَبْصِرَةً وذِكْرى﴾ [Qāf: 8], that is: We did that in order to give insight by it and to point to the power. Then He said: ﴿لِكُلِّ عَبْدٍ مُنِيبٍ﴾ [Qāf: 8], that is: for every servant who turns back to Allah and reflects on His power.

zajjaj:9-9.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَحَبَّ الحَصِيدِ﴾, that is: and We caused to grow in it the grain that is harvested; so He gathered by that everything that serves as staple food, of the grain of wheat and barley and everything that is harvested.

zajjaj:24-24.t:
His saying: ﴿ألْقِيا في جَهَنَّمَ كُلَّ كَفّارٍ عَنِيدٍ﴾, that is: who stubbornly deviated from the truth.
His saying: ﴿ألْقِيا﴾: the right view in my opinion — and Allah knows best — is that it is a command to the two angels, because ﴿ألْقِيا﴾ is for two. Some grammarians said that the Arabs command one person with the dual form, saying: "قُوما واضْرِبا زَيْدًا يا رَجُلُ" (stand, [you two], and strike Zayd, O man). They related that al-Ḥajjāj used to say: "يا حَرَسِي اضْرِبا عُنُقَهُ" (O guard, strike [you two] his neck). They said: that is said only because most of what the Arabs say to someone they command is in the dual form, such as:
؎خَلِيلَيَّ مُرّا بِي عَلى أُمِّ جُنْدَبٍ
(My two friends, take me past Umm Jundab.)
؎قِفا نَبْكِ مِن ذِكْرى حَبِيبٍ ومَنزِلِ
(Stop, [you two], let us weep at the memory of a beloved and a dwelling.)
Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] said: this is a verb put in the dual for emphasis (tawkīd), as though when He said "ألْقِيا" it stood in place of His saying "ألْقِ، ألْقِ" (cast, cast); likewise in his view "قِفا" means "قِفْ، قِفْ" (stop, stop), so it stood in place of two verbs and was formed [in the dual]. This is a sound view, but I hold that it is a command to two — and Allah knows best.

zajjaj:27-27.t: His saying: ﴿قالَ قَرِينُهُ رَبَّنا ما أطْغَيْتُهُ ولَكِنْ كانَ في ضَلالٍ بَعِيدٍ﴾: the meaning is: he only transgressed through his own misguidance; I only called him and he responded, as He said: ﴿وَقالَ الشَّيْطانُ لَمّا قُضِيَ الأمْرُ إنَّ اللَّهَ وعَدَكم وعْدَ الحَقِّ ووَعَدْتُكم فَأخْلَفْتُكم وما كانَ لِي عَلَيْكم مِن سُلْطانٍ إلا أنْ دَعَوْتُكم فاسْتَجَبْتُمْ لِي﴾ [Ibrāhīm: 22]

zajjaj:29-29.t: His saying: ﴿ما يُبَدَّلُ القَوْلُ لَدَيَّ وما أنا بِظَلامٍ لِلْعَبِيدِ﴾, that is: whoever does a good deed shall have ten like it, and whoever does an evil deed shall be recompensed only with its like.

zajjaj:30-30.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَوْمَ نَقُولُ لِجَهَنَّمَ هَلِ امْتَلأْتِ﴾ — and it has been read: "يَوْمَ يَقُولُ لِجَهَنَّمَ" (the day He will say to Hell). "يَوْمَ" is accusative in two ways: in the sense of "the word is not changed with Me on that day", and in the sense of "warn them of the day We will say to Hell", as He said: ﴿وَأنْذِرْهم يَوْمَ الحَسْرَةِ إذْ قُضِيَ الأمْرُ﴾ [Maryam: 39]. His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿هَلِ امْتَلأْتِ﴾, that is: "or have you not become full?" The question is only a rebuke to those who are made to enter it, an increase in what they abhor, and a proof of the truth of His saying: ﴿لأمْلأنَّ جَهَنَّمَ مِنكَ ومِمَّنْ تَبِعَكَ مِنهم أجْمَعِينَ﴾ [Ṣād: 85]. As for His saying: ﴿وَتَقُولُ هَلْ مِن مَزِيدٍ﴾, there are two aspects in it according to the people of the language. One of them is that it says that after being filled, saying: ﴿هَلْ مِن مَزِيدٍ﴾, that is: "is there any place left in me that has not been filled?", that is: I have become full. Another aspect: it says "هَلْ مِن مَزِيدٍ" out of fury against those who disobeyed, as He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿سَمِعُوا لَها تَغَيُّظًا وزَفِيرًا﴾ [al-Furqān: 12]. As for this speech of it and its addressing, Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, has placed in it that by which it discerns and speaks, just as He placed in what He created that it glorifies Him with His praise, and as He placed in the ant that it said: ﴿يا أيُّها النَّمْلُ ادْخُلُوا مَساكِنَكُمْ﴾ [al-Naml: 18]. Some people have claimed that it became full, so that its appearance became the appearance of one who, had it discernment, would say: ﴿هَلْ مِن مَزِيدٍ﴾, as the poet said:
؎اِمْتَلَأ الحَوْضُ وقالَ قُطْنِي ∗∗∗ مَهْلًا رُوَيْدًا قَدْ مَلَأْتَ بَطْنِي
(The basin filled and said: Enough for me! Gently, slowly, you have filled my belly.)
— and there was no speech there. But this does not resemble that, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, has informed us that created things glorify [Him] and that we do not understand their glorification; if it were only that they indicate that they are created, we would understand their glorification.

zajjaj:35-35.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَهم ما يَشاءُونَ فِيها ولَدَيْنا مَزِيدٌ﴾: the meaning is: they have in it whatever they wish, and with Us is more, of what has not occurred to their hearts. It has come in the tafsīr (exegesis) that clouds pass over the people of the Garden and rain houris upon them, and the houris say: "We are those of whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَلَدَيْنا مَزِيدٌ﴾
[Translator's note: the opening quotation mark in the source is not closed.]

zajjaj:36-36.t:
﴿وَكَمْ أهْلَكْنا قَبْلَهم مِن قَرْنٍ هم أشَدُّ مِنهم بَطْشًا﴾: people have differed about the qarn (generation). (Some said: the qarn is ten years; some said: thirty years; some said: forty years; some said: seventy years; they also said: a hundred years; and some said: a hundred and twenty years. The qarn — and Allah knows best — is the measure of the average lifespan of the people of an age; so the qarn among the people of Noah is according to the measure of their lifespans. Its derivation is from "اَلِاقْتِرانُ" (being joined together), so it is as though it is the measure which is the greatest span in which the people of that age are joined together in their survival.
[Translator's note: the opening parenthesis in the source is not closed.]
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَنَقَّبُوا في البِلادِ هَلْ مِن مَحِيصٍ﴾: it has been read "فَنَقَبُوا", with doubling and without doubling. The meaning is: "they went round and searched, but saw no escape from death". Imruʾ al-Qays said:
؎لَقَدْ نَقَّبْتُ في الآفاقِ حَتّى ∗∗∗ رَضِيتُ مِنَ الغَنِيمَةِ بِالإيابِ
(I have roamed through the horizons until I was content to take, as my booty, the return home.)
It is also read: "فَنَقِّبُوا في البِلادِ" (so search through the lands), that is: "search and look". From this comes "نَقِيبُ القَوْمِ" (the naqīb of the people) for the one who knows their affairs, like "اَلْعَرِّيفُ" (the overseer).

zajjaj:37-37.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إنَّ في ذَلِكَ لَذِكْرى لِمَن كانَ لَهُ قَلْبٌ أوْ ألْقى السَّمْعَ وهو شَهِيدٌ﴾ — and it has been read: "أوْ أُلْقِيَ السَّمْعُ" (or hearing is given). The meaning of "مَن كانَ لَهُ قَلْبٌ" is: whoever turns his heart to understanding. Do you not see that His saying ﴿صُمٌّ بُكْمٌ عُمْيٌ﴾ [al-Baqara: 18] [means] that they did not listen as one who seeks to understand and seeks guidance, so they were treated as one who did not hear? As the poet said:
؎أصَمُّ عَمّا ساءَهُ سَمِيعُ
(Deaf to what displeases him, yet hearing.)
The meaning of ﴿أوْ ألْقى السَّمْعَ﴾ is: he listened and did not occupy his heart with anything other than what he hears. The Arabs say: "ألْقِ إلَيَّ سَمْعَكَ" (lend me your hearing), that is: listen to me. The meaning of ﴿وَهُوَ شَهِيدٌ﴾ is: while his heart is in what he hears. It has come in the tafsīr (exegesis) that by it the People of the Book are meant, who had with them the description of the Prophet ﷺ; so the meaning according to this tafsīr of ﴿أوْ ألْقى السَّمْعَ وهو شَهِيدٌ﴾ is that the description of the Prophet, upon him be peace, is in his book.

zajjaj:38-38.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنا السَّماواتِ والأرْضَ وما بَيْنَهُما في سِتَّةِ أيّامٍ وما مَسَّنا مِن لُغُوبٍ﴾: "اَللُّغُوبُ" is tiredness and exhaustion; one says "لَغَبَ، يَلْغُبُ، لُغُوبًا". This — according to what has been mentioned — is because the Jews, may they be cursed, said: "Allah created the heavens and the earth in six days, the first of them Sunday and the last of them Friday, and rested on the Sabbath. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that He created them in six days, and He is glorified and exalted above being described with tiredness or fatigue.
[Translator's note: the opening quotation mark in the source is not closed.]

zajjaj:39-39.t: Then He said: ﴿فاصْبِرْ عَلى ما يَقُولُونَ وسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ قَبْلَ طُلُوعِ الشَّمْسِ وقَبْلَ الغُرُوبِ﴾: by "قَبْلَ طُلُوعِ الشَّمْسِ" (before sunrise) He means the dawn prayer, and by "وَقَبْلَ الغُرُوبِ" (and before sunset) the afternoon (ʿaṣr) prayer.

zajjaj:40-40.t: ﴿وَمِنَ اللَّيْلِ فَسَبِّحْهُ﴾: the sunset (maghrib) prayer; ﴿وَأدْبارَ السُّجُودِ﴾: the two rakʿas after the sunset prayer, on this view. It is also possible that it is a command to glorify after finishing the prayer. It is read: ﴿وَمِنَ اللَّيْلِ فَسَبِّحْهُ وأدْبارَ السُّجُودِ﴾ and "إدْبارَ السُّجُودِ". Whoever reads "وَأدْبارَ", with fatḥa on the alif, it is the plural of "دُبُرٌ" (end, back); and whoever reads "وإدْبارَ", it is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of "أدْبَرَ، يُدْبِرُ، إدْبارًا".

zajjaj:41-41.t: His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿واسْتَمِعْ يَوْمَ يُنادِ المُنادِ مِن مَكانٍ قَرِيبٍ﴾: It has come in the tafsīr (exegesis) that what is meant by it is that the call to the Gathering is made from a near place. It was said: it is the Rock which is in Jerusalem (Bayt al-Maqdis), and it is said that it is in the middle of the earth.

zajjaj:42-42.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ذَلِكَ يَوْمُ الخُرُوجِ﴾, that is: the day they are raised and brought out. Like it is ﴿يَوْمَ يَدْعُ الدّاعِ إلى شَيْءٍ نُكُرٍ﴾ [al-Qamar: 6] ﴿خُشَّعًا أبْصارُهم يَخْرُجُونَ مِنَ الأجْداثِ كَأنَّهم جَرادٌ مُنْتَشِرٌ﴾ [al-Qamar: 7]; "اَلْأجْداثُ" are the graves. Abū ʿUbayda said: "يَوْمُ الخُرُوجِ" (the Day of Coming Forth) is one of the names of the Day of Resurrection, and he cited as evidence the saying of al-ʿAjjāj:
؎ألَيْسَ يَوْمٌ سُمِّيَ الخُرُوجا ∗∗∗ أعْظَمَ يَوْمٍ رَجَّةً رَجُوجا؟
(Is not a day named "the Coming Forth" the greatest of days in convulsion, violently shaking?)

zajjaj:45-45.t: His saying: ﴿وَما أنْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ بِجَبّارٍ فَذَكِّرْ بِالقُرْآنِ مَن يَخافُ وعِيدِ﴾: this is as He said: ﴿لَسْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ بِمُصَيْطِرٍ﴾ [al-Ghāshiya: 22]. This was before the Prophet ﷺ was commanded to fight, because Sūrat "ق" is Meccan.
